content: 1. Ospemifene and esterified estrogens exhibit pharmacodynamic synergism, leading to increased effects of each other. Their coadministration is contraindicated. 2. Esterified estrogens reduce the effects of anastrozole through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated as estrogen may diminish the pharmacologic action of anastrozole. Coadministration is not recommended. 3. Esterified estrogens decrease the effects of antithrombin alfa via pharmacodynamic antagonism, increasing the risk of thromboembolic disorders. This combination is contraindicated. 4. Apalutamide reduces the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, monitor for therapeutic loss and adjust the dose as per prescribing information. 5. Enzalutamide decreases the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 6. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 7. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 8. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 9. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 10. Etrasimod and esterified estrogens may enhance each other's immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 11. Fexinidazole increases the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 12. Givosiran increases the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the dose of CYP1A2 substrates as per product labeling. 13. Idelalisib increases the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 14. Ivosidenib decreases the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, monitor for therapeutic loss and adjust the dose accordingly. 15. Lorlatinib decreases the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 16. Tucatinib increases the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the dose of CYP3A4 substrates as per product labeling. 17. Esterified estrogens reduce the effects of albiglutide through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor glycemic control in diabetic patients. 18. Amobarbital decreases the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 19. Aprepitant increases the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 20. Artemether/lumefantrine decreases the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 21. Atazanavir may increase or decrease the levels of esterified estrogens by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Use alternatives if available. 22. Belzutifan decreases the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. If coadministration is unavoidable, consider increasing the dose of CYP3A4 substrates as per prescribing information. 23. Bosentan decreases the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 24. Butabarbital decreases the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 25. Carbamazepine decreases the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 26. Cenobamate decreases the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Increase the dose of CYP3A4 substrates as needed. 27. Ceritinib increases the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 28. Chloramphenicol increases the levels of esterified estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for increased side effects. 29. Diltiazem increases the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 40. Dronedarone increases the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 41. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 42. Elagolix decreases the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Consider increasing the dose of CYP3A substrates if needed. 43. Encorafenib both inhibits and induces CYP3A4 at clinically relevant plasma concentrations, potentially increasing toxicity or reducing efficacy of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates. Use caution and monitor. 44. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 45. Griseofulvin decreases the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 46. Esterified estrogens reduce the effects of hemin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor. Drugs that increase delta-aminolevulinic acid synthetase may decrease hemin efficacy. 47. Esterified estrogens reduce the effects of hyaluronidase by rendering tissues partially resistant to its action when given in large systemic doses. Patients may require larger amounts of hyaluronidase for equivalent dispersing effects. Use caution and monitor. 48. Hydrocortisone decreases the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 49. Iloperidone increases the levels of esterified estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 50. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 51. Istradefylline increases the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. At 40 mg/day, it increased peak levels and AUC of CYP3A4 substrates in clinical trials. Consider dose reduction of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates. 52. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 53. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 54. Esterified estrogens decrease lamotrigine levels by increasing hepatic clearance, potentially reducing lamotrigine levels by almost 50%. Use caution and monitor.
